name: Steps
summary: Show progress through a sequence of ordered stages — wizards, onboarding, checkouts — rendered through the shared Steps.
lead: Steps carries a progress state machine, horizontal/vertical layouts and clickable navigation — too much to rebuild as a web component, so it stays on real Ant: antd v6 (React) and ant-design-vue v4 (Vue), both themed once by the shared stepsTheme. Two implementations, one DS V3 look. This is the composite half of the hybrid.

props.name: current
props.desc: Zero-based index of the active step

props.name: onChange
props.desc: Fires when a step is clicked (if navigable)

whenToUse.when: a linear sequence of stages where the user should see where they are and what's left
peer views the user switches between freely — no order, no progress
a single continuous completion metric, not discrete named stages

opinion.note: Keep titles to a short noun phrase per stage. Reserve Steps for genuinely ordered flows — if the sections have no order, use Tabs. Show a description only when the title alone is ambiguous.

snippets.label: HTML
snippets.note: Composite has no framework-free element, so its paste-and-run form is a CDN-React page — React + antd load from a CDN and mount on open, consuming the same shared stepsTheme. No build step.

codeNote: React and Vue are two real vendor libraries at two Ant generations — they can't share a primitive. They converge via the same token/theme (stepsTheme); residual drift is caught by visual regression.

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Composite shown as a CDN-React page mounted at #react-root; the measure reads the real antd v6 Steps bound to stepsTheme.
